title: You probably skipped her.
paragraphs: A single line… tucked into the closing words of a letter most people rush past.
“Give my greetings to the brothers at Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church in her house.” — Nympha

No backstory.
No miracle attached to her name.
No spotlight.
a church was breathing, praying, repenting, and worshiping inside her home.
You’ve read bigger names. Louder stories. Apostles who shook cities.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
the Gospel didn’t spread only through pulpits.
Just oil lamps flickering against the walls.
And in the middle of it all—
Because hosting a church wasn’t safe.
This wasn’t a Bible study with snacks and comfort.
This was allegiance to Christ in a world that could turn on you.
You open your home, you open your life.
And here’s the part that hits harder than it should:
You’ve wanted to do something “big” for God.
She didn’t wait for a platform.
“Each one should use whatever gift he has received to serve others, faithfully administering God’s grace in its various forms.” — 1 Peter 4:10
Not what you wish you had.
Not what you think is enough.
A single line became eternal evidence.
You say you’re waiting for clarity.
But what if obedience is already clear?
But what if readiness comes after surrender?
You say your life is too ordinary.
But what if God builds His kingdom through what you call ordinary?
“Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” — Hebrews 13:2
It’s participation in the mission of God.
Because opening your door means dying to yourself.
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
That quiet pull to use what you have for something more eternal.
To create space for God to move.
And now her name is written in Scripture.
Here’s the tension you can’t escape:
There are two futures in front of you.
One where your life stays contained, safe, untouched—
and one where your obedience costs you something…
Jesus didn’t die so your faith could stay private.
“By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.” — John 13:35
It’s not about earning your place by doing more.
It’s about what Christ already did.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” — Ephesians 2:8
You don’t open your life to be saved.
You open your life because you are.
So now it’s your turn to face it.
What has God already placed in your hands?
What are you withholding that could become someone else’s encounter with Him?
If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Say it plainly—“Lord, I’ll use what You gave me.”
And don’t keep this to yourself.
There’s someone you know who keeps waiting for “the right time.”
Follow this journey if you want deeper truth that actually confronts and transforms.
